title: Morphisms to an etale space are open graphs
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and let $X,Y,B$ be algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] with maps $X\to B$ and $Y\to B$. Suppose $Y\to B$ is chartwise etale [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence], without requiring it to be representable. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], point spaces have the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology], and open subspaces mean [def-a1-space-open-subspace]. Sending a $B$-morphism $a:X\to Y$ to its graph gives a bijection between $\operatorname{Hom}_B(X,Y)$ and open subspaces $\Gamma\subseteq X\times_BY$ for which $\Gamma\to X$ is surjective and universally injective on point spaces. Universally injective means that its point map is injective after every algebraic-space base change; surjectivity likewise holds after every such base change. For each such $\Gamma$, its projection $\Gamma\to X$ is an isomorphism, and the inverse correspondence is $\operatorname{pr}_Y\circ(\Gamma\to X)^{-1}$. These correspondences commute with arbitrary base change in $B$. No quasi-compactness, separation or quasi-separatedness is assumed on $X,Y,B$.

source.place: Rydh, author version 2010-03-03, Appendix A, Corollary (A.3) and Proposition (A.2), printed p.35. The no-quasi-separatedness form follows from the same chartwise facts; Stacks spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 05W5 (lemma-etale-universally-injective-open) proves the converse without that convention. Read online; local Rydh PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Put $P=X\times_BY$, with projection $p:P\to X$; this is an algebraic space by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], and $p$ is chartwise etale by the arbitrary-base-change clause of [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]. For a $B$-map $a:X\to Y$, its graph $s:X\to P$ is the natural map $x\mapsto(x,a(x))$ and satisfies $ps=\mathrm{id}_X$. Both $X\to X$ and $P\to X$ are chartwise etale; the over-base clause of that permanence node makes $s$ chartwise etale. The formula shows that $s$ is injective on sections over every scheme. Apply [lem-sfb-space-etale-monomorphism-open] to $s$. Its open image is the subfunctor $\Gamma_a(H)=\{(x,a_H(x)):x\in X(H)\}$, and $p|_{\Gamma_a}$ has inverse $x\mapsto(x,a_H(x))$ on each test scheme. Thus it is an isomorphism and remains so after every algebraic-space base change; in particular its point map is always bijective.

source.place: Tags 03FU (lemma-base-change-etale), 03FV (lemma-etale-permanence); spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 05W5 (lemma-etale-universally-injective-open), monomorphism case. Rydh Corollary (A.3), forward direction, with Proposition (A.2)(ii).

proof.text: Conversely let $j:\Gamma\hookrightarrow P$ be an open subspace as in the statement, and put $q=pj:\Gamma\to X$. By [def-a1-space-open-subspace], all scheme tests of $j$ are open immersions. The last clause of [lem-a1-space-open-chart-tests] says precisely that composing $j$ with an etale scheme chart of $\Gamma$ is representable etale. Thus $j$ is chartwise etale. Composition in [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence] makes $q$ chartwise etale. The assumed universal injectivity and universal surjectivity of $q$ have not been replaced by representability.

source.place: Tag 02WK (lemma-composition-representable-transformations-property), open chart tests; spaces-properties.tex Tag 03FT (lemma-composition-etale).

proof.text: Put $R=\Gamma\times_X\Gamma$ using [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], with first projection $r:R\to\Gamma$ and diagonal $\delta:\Gamma\to R$. Universal injectivity of $q$ says in particular that $|r|$ is injective, since $r$ is the base change of $q$ by $q:\Gamma\to X$. For any $z\in|R|$, the identity $r\delta=\mathrm{id}_\Gamma$ gives $|r|(|\delta|(|r|(z)))=|r|(z)$. Injectivity of $|r|$ implies $|\delta|(|r|(z))=z$. Thus $|\delta|$ is surjective. This proves the needed consequence of universal injectivity directly on point sets, without assuming that point spaces preserve fibre products.

source.place: Tag 040X (lemma-universally-injective), (2) implies (3): the split-injective point-map argument is explicit.

proof.text: The first projection $r:R\to\Gamma$ is a base change of $q$ and hence chartwise etale by [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]. Since $r\delta=\mathrm{id}_\Gamma$, its over-base clause makes $\delta$ chartwise etale. The formula $z\mapsto(z,z)$ is injective on all scheme sections, so [lem-sfb-space-etale-monomorphism-open] makes $\delta$ a representable open immersion. Identify its source with its image subfunctor. Step 3 and the full-point-image clause of [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] imply that this image is all of $R$, so $\delta$ is an isomorphism. For any scheme $H$ and $u,v\in\Gamma(H)$ with $q_H(u)=q_H(v)$, the pair $(u,v)\in R(H)$ is therefore $(w,w)$ for a unique $w\in\Gamma(H)$. Hence $u=v$ and $q$ is a sheaf monomorphism. Apply [lem-sfb-space-etale-monomorphism-open] again, now to $q$. It is an open immersion, and its point map is surjective by hypothesis. The same full-point-image clause identifies its open image with $X$. Therefore $q$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 05W5 (lemma-etale-universally-injective-open), diagonal argument, with spaces-properties.tex Tag 03BZ (lemma-open-subspaces).

proof.text: Define $a=\operatorname{pr}_Y\circ j\circ q^{-1}:X\to Y$. The fibre-product equation and $q q^{-1}=\mathrm{id}_X$ make this a $B$-morphism. On every scheme $H$, the inclusion $j$ is $(q,\operatorname{pr}_Yj)$, so $j q^{-1}$ is $(\mathrm{id}_X,a)$. Its image subfunctor is exactly $\Gamma_a$ and equals the original $\Gamma$, since $q^{-1}$ is an isomorphism. Conversely the projection of the graph of a given $a$ has inverse $x\mapsto(x,a(x))$, and composing with its second projection recovers $a$. These two explicit identities prove the asserted bijection and the formula for its inverse; equality here is equality of subfunctors, not a choice of a representative open immersion.

source.place: Corollary (A.3), explicit inverse of the graph correspondence; agent-written assembly of the sheaf fibre-product formulas.

proof.text: Let $b:B_1\to B$ be arbitrary and write $X_1=X\times_BB_1$, $Y_1=Y\times_BB_1$. On a test scheme, the canonical identification $P\times_BB_1\cong X_1\times_{B_1}Y_1$ sends $((x,y),t)$ to $((x,t),(y,t))$, with inverse forgetting the repeated $t$. Under it, the pullback of $\Gamma_a$ consists precisely of $((x,t),(a(x),t))$, the graph of $a_1$. An open subspace remains open under this pullback: for a scheme $H\to P\times_BB_1$ its scheme test is the same open subscheme as the test $H\to P$, by [def-a1-space-open-subspace]. Moreover the inverse of the pulled-back isomorphism $q_1$ is $(q^{-1})_1$, because pulling back $q q^{-1}=\mathrm{id}$ and $q^{-1}q=\mathrm{id}$ gives the two inverse identities. Its second projection therefore recovers exactly $a_1$. This proves base-change compatibility in both directions, including preservation of the required universal point conditions.

source.place: Corollary (A.3), functoriality written out using the sheaf fibre-product universal property.

lean.statement: theorem space_etale_open_graph {S : Scheme.{u}} {X Y B : AlgebraicSpace S} (f : X ⟶ B) (g : Y ⟶ B) (hg : IsChartwiseEtale g) : (∀ a : {a : X ⟶ Y // a ≫ g = f}, ∃ A : OpenSubspace (enlargedFibreProduct f g), A.val = etaleGraphSubfunctor f g a ∧ EtaleGraphPointCondition f g A) ∧ (∀ A : OpenSubspace (enlargedFibreProduct f g), EtaleGraphPointCondition f g A → (∃! a : {a : X ⟶ Y // a ≫ g = f}, etaleGraphSubfunctor f g a = A.val) ∧ ∃ e : A.val.toFunctor ≅ X.obj.obj, e.hom = A.val.ι ≫ (Limits.pullback.fst f.hom g.hom).hom ∧ ∀ a : {a : X ⟶ Y // a ≫ g = f}, etaleGraphSubfunctor f g a = A.val → a.val.hom.hom = e.inv ≫ A.val.ι ≫ (Limits.pullback.snd f.hom g.hom).hom)
